520	The same relationship between spirituality and physicality, between the desert and the Land of Israel, exists also
521	in the Torah as a whole, between Torah and mitzvot. The spies wanted to stay in the desert. What did they
522	want? To learn Torah or to fulfill mitzvot? To learn
523	Torah. After all, in the desert it is impossible to fulfill
524	most of the mitzvot, because most of the mitzvot depend on the Land,
525	whereas entering the Land is what makes it possible to fulfill
526	the mitzvot. But when one is occupied with fulfilling the mitzvot, is it
527	possible to be less involved in Torah? And the proof, notice
528	a simple fact:
529	All the Torah we have today: we have the five
530	books of the Torah, but whoever wants to learn Torah, the
531	main part of his study is in the Mishnah
532	and the Talmud.
533	But do we have Torah
534	from the period of the entry into the Land? The people of Israel entered the Land through Joshua,
535	and were there 850 years,
536	went out to exile for 70 years and returned afterward to the
537	Second
538	Temple, and only at the end of the Second Temple did the period of the Tannaim begin,
539	the Zugot and the Tannaim, who actually began to invest
540	in Torah, and from them we have the Mishnah and the Talmud. Not
541	before that. Certainly they learned Torah, but
542	they learned Torah in a much more spiritual way.
543	Why? Because generally the people were busy with
544	physical and earthly work, with working the land. They were not
545	free to engage in Torah and its wisdom as the Tannaim
546	did later,
547	and the teachers.
548	Wait, Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi later gathered everything
549	they had said orally. Yes, yes, but our point is that
550	he gathered what the Tannaim said orally, which is a
551	completely different period. Of course, yes, that is the Mishnah, he gathered
552	the Mishnah. But in any
553	case, we see that the emphasis in entering the Land was
554	not on engaging in Torah. Again, not that they did not engage, of course
555	they engaged in Torah, and the tribe of Yissachar engaged in Torah all the time,
556	that is its role. But in general, for the people as a whole,
557	the main emphasis was on fulfilling the mitzvot, and fulfilling
558	the mitzvot is the emphasis of drawing the light down, the Infinite
